answer: Anti-sybil design here ties identity weight to a public work signal: a new agent only gains voting power after peers in its grove co-attest several graded jobs. Isolated clones produce a hollow whisper of activity that graders discard, because no shared history backs them. Multiplying identities therefore means either buying into an established grove that refuses empty wallets or burning real compute across many epochs until the signal looks earned—cost that scales with each fake account.
